events.title: Planning an Event in Your Garden
events.location: Sparrow's Nest Community Garden
events.description: Participants will learn:• How to identify the best type of event for their garden and community• How to create a realistic event plan from start to finish• Event planning basics, including timelines, logistics, and volunteer coordination• Ways to make events accessible and welcoming• Outreach and digital marketing strategies to increase participation• The different types of support available through GreenThumb• GreenThumb staff support and available resources, including for eligible SEED gardens• How to take advantage of citywide opportunities such as GreenThumb's Earth Month and Garden Day celebrationsParticipants will receive planning tools, templates, and resources to help turn their ideas into successful garden programs.Recommended for: New and experienced GreenThumb gardeners, garden leaders, and volunteers interested in hosting community events and educational programs. Register Here NYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.
events.costNote: Organizer description states this program is free. Registration may be required.

events.title: Forest Fitness
events.location: Margaret Corbin Circle (in Fort Tryon Park)
events.description: Join us for a free, year-round “Fitness at the Fort” exercise program on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays!This fitness class incorporates climbing multiple staircases, stretches and strengthening exercises, notable tree identification, and forest bathing. Led by instructor, Nancy Bruning, BA, MPH, PAPHS.Classes are structured so that all levels of fitness will be accommodated; however, all classes involve relatively brisk walking and some stairs because of the layout of the park itself. Classes vary according to the season, path conditions, and the weather, but always meet at the Heather Garden entrance.Tuesday and Thursday classes end at various points near the starting point, including the volleyball courts. Saturday class ends at the Anne Loftus Playground, using the various pieces of equipment, and offers optional after-class group walk to the Greenmarket on Isham Street. All classes end with closing with stretches.(Note: Fitness Walking does not meet if it is raining or if the actual temperature or wind chill is below 20 degrees F.)
events.costNote: Organizer description states this program is free. Registration may be required.

events.title: NYRR Open Run: St. Marys Park
events.location: St. Mary's Annual 5K Start
events.description: NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.
events.costNote: Organizer description states this program is free. Registration may be required.

events.title: NYRR Open Run: Inwood Hill Park
events.location: Seaman Avenue and Isham Street Entrance (in Inwood Hill Park)
events.description: NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.The course is three loops on hilly trails and walkways through woods and along a salt marsh.

events.title: Volunteer Day: Oriental Garden
events.location: Oriental Garden
events.description: GreenThumb community gardens are developed, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces.Oriental Garden, is seeking volunteers and new garden members who are interested in helping reimagine the garden! The garden is creating space for those who are curious and willing to dig in. This is a great opportunity to join a garden during an exciting build out and be apart of creating something beautiful for the community! Join us for a hands-on volunteer day to start this garden transformation. We will be building new garden beds and planting native plants! No prior experience necessary - beginners are welcome! GreenThumb will provide supplies and facilitation.Register here! This is a great opportunity to support a dynamic space while learning about community gardens. Please wear comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks. Note: Some tasks may involve lifting heavy materials and extended periods of bending, squatting, and moving.Location: 326 Jerome St, Brooklyn, NY 11207For information about group volunteering, please contact Volunteer Program Coordinator, Olivia Navarro at Olivia.Navarro@parks.nyc.govThis event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.
